headline: Deep learning maps omics and histology data onto molecular and clinical endpoints
label: Deep Learning Biomedical Prediction
summary: Recent preprints and publications apply self-supervised and semi-supervised objectives to exploit unlabeled tumor and single-cell data for prediction.
synthesis: The dominant thread is deep learning that maps one data modality onto a biological or clinical target: histology onto gene expression (HistoPrism) and cell-type abundance (Hist2Cell), transcriptomes onto protein and phosphoprotein abundance (DeepGxP), and cfDNA fragment profiles onto cancer detection (DeepFRAG). A second strand uses semi-supervised or self-supervised objectives to exploit unlabeled data, as in Cox-MT for TCGA survival models, scAURA for scRNA-seq clustering, and SRNC for novel cell-type identification. Several entries emphasize explicit benchmarking, including HistoPrism's pathway-level test and scAURA's evaluation on 18 datasets against 13 methods. The structural variant filtering benchmark reports that a simple Random Forest matches ResNet, diffusion, and ensemble models. The set is heterogeneous, and the evidence is largely method-level rather than mechanistic.
